title: Bloodline Resonance
next_chapter_hook: Chen Nian's warning exploded like thunderclap in his mind, and on that ancestral tablet deep within the shrine that had never been illuminated, a name that made Chen Ji's entire body turn to ice was unmistakably inscribed—

text.content:
The ethereal glow of the fragment receded like an ebbing tide. Chen Ji knelt on one knee, cold sweat beading at his temples. He could feel subtle yet terrifying changes rippling through his body—molten magma seemed to surge through his veins, every meridian violently trembling, as if an existence that had slumbered for ten thousand years was awakening.

"Cough..." He coughed lightly, raising his eyes to look toward where Ling Yuan had vanished. That gaze carried meanings too complex—既有scrutinizing，又有某种难以言喻的expectant. It wasn't the look one gave an enemy, but rather... a treasure lost and found again.

Chen Ji clenched his fists abruptly, his knuckles whitening. That momentary exchange had stirred an inexplicable flutter in his heart, as if some long-sealed memories were about to break free from the earth.

The Tianji Record Fragment suddenly vibrated on its own, golden patterns writhing across its surface like living creatures, bursting with blinding light. Before Chen Ji could react, a torrential stream of information flooded into his Mental Sea like a bursting dam—the visions were not glimpses of the future, but far more ancient fragments of memory.

The images were blurry and fragmented, yet carried an authenticity that resonated from deep within his bloodline. He saw a grand ancestral hall standing amidst clouds and mist, three ancient seal characters on its plaque emanating a primordial aura—Chen Family Shrine.

"How is this possible..." Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply, his fingertips trembling involuntarily. He was an orphan, raised by the Tianqing Sect since childhood, never knowing his own bloodline origins. Yet the familiar sensation surging through his blood told him this was all real.

The interior of the ancestral hall grew increasingly clear. Dozens of memorial tablets were neatly arranged on the incense table, incense smoke curling, candlelight flickering. The names inscribed on those tablets had become illegible, yet Chen Ji could sense the profound heritage contained within each one—accumulated fortune and legacy passed down through generations.

His gaze was firmly captured by a figure's back before the memorial tablets. The person wore a blackish-green robe, their posture straight as a pine, hands clasped behind their back, gazing at the innermost shrine of the ancestral hall. Though he couldn't see the face, the familiar posture and aura made Chen Ji almost certain—

"Ling Yuan..." he murmured, his voice hoarse unlike his own. Why would this person appear in the Chen Family Shrine? Why did he look at Chen Ji with such complicated eyes? Countless questions coiled around his heart like venomous snakes.

dialogue.content:
"Young Master, you've finally seen it..." A weathered voice rang out in his Mental Sea, carrying an unmistakable mix of relief and sorrow.

Chen Ji whirled around to find Mo Xiansheng's phantom suspended in mid-air, his wrinkled face contorted with complex emotions.

"What do you know?" Chen Ji demanded sharply, his voice laced with suppressed fury. "What is my relationship with Ling Yuan? What is the truth behind the Chen family's destruction?"

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng's phantom fell silent for a moment, his gaze flickering with struggle. Finally, he spoke slowly: "This old servant dares not speak. Your father left a dying order before his death—the secrets of the Tianji Record can only be discovered by the Young Master yourself. But this old servant can tell you one thing—Ling Yuan... his original name was Chen Yuan, and he is your true uncle."

These four words exploded like thunderclap in Chen Ji's mind, his body swaying violently, nearly falling again. Uncle? That old Sect Leader who appeared to shelter him while harboring malicious intentions—was actually his blood relative?

"No wonder... no wonder his obsession with the Tianji Record runs so deep." Chen Ji murmured to himself, instantly piecing together many things. The Tianji Record's inheritance had always selected only from within Chen bloodline—Ling Yuan was chosen yet abandoned. This resentment was enough to drive a man to madness.

The burning sensation in his bloodline grew increasingly intense. Chen Ji felt as if he were inside a furnace. More memory fragments flashed by like a carousel—he saw a少年in magnificent robes kneeling before the ancestral hall accepting the test, saw the Tianji Record's light fall upon another young man, saw the disqualified one's eyes shift from anticipation to despair, and from despair to deepest hatred.

"I was chosen, while he was rejected." Chen Ji finally understood everything. "So he hates me, hates the Tianji Record, hates everything."

But was it truly that simple? Chen Ji had been bullied endlessly in the Sect since childhood, never enjoying any of the honors that should have come with Chen bloodline. Was all this fate messing with him, or was someone secretly manipulating everything?

choice.prompt: The memory fragments from his bloodline awakening left Chen Ji in momentary chaos, but he quickly calmed his heart. Now he needed to decide his next move—investigate the truth of his origins while the iron was hot, or temporarily lie low and observe covertly?

choices.description: While the bloodline memories remain warm, trace the investigation into the truth of the Chen family's destruction and Ling Yuan's past. Cannot allow this heartache to become a fatal weakness in the future.
choices.visible_cost: May alert the target, causing Ling Yuan to become vigilant
choices.visible_reward: Gain critical information about the Chen family and the Tianji Record's inheritance
choices.risk_hint: Ling Yuan is an old schemer; rash action may fall into his trap

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. He raised his head to look at Mo Xiansheng's phantom, his gaze carrying unshakable resolve: "What exactly happened the night the Chen family was destroyed? How did my parents die?"

Mo Xiansheng's phantom trembled violently, as if touching upon some past he refused to recall. He opened his mouth, yet hesitated.

"Young Master, some truths... are you certain you wish to know?" The old man's voice was low and trembling. "Once known, there is no turning back."

choices.description: Now is not the time to settle accounts. Ling Yuan's depths are unfathomable; rash action will only expose our cards. Better to lay plans covertly, waiting for the perfect moment to strike with lethal force.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the best opportunity to unravel the mystery of one's origins
choices.visible_reward: Hide strength, prevent Ling Yuan from noticing our awakening, maintain information advantage
choices.risk_hint: The truth may be forever sealed away, the heartache may become a hidden danger in the future

text.content:
Chen Ji closed his eyes, forcibly suppressing the churning emotions. When he opened them again after a moment, those eyes had returned to their usual calmness and depth.

"I understand." He said lightly. "Mo Xiansheng, these matters... let us discuss them later."

Mo Xiansheng hesitated briefly, then revealed an approving expression: "The Young Master can endure what others cannot—this is truly a blessing. This old servant will guard these secrets for you, awaiting only the opportune moment."

He paused, lowering his voice to add: "But the Young Master must be careful—Chen Xuan... is not as simple as you might imagine."

Chen Xuan? This name made Chen Ji's heart tighten. The first holder of the Tianji Record, that legendary supreme expert—why would Mo Xiansheng suddenly mention him at this moment?

Just as he wished to press further, the burning sensation in his bloodline suddenly surged violently. An unprecedented power erupted from the depths of his heart, spreading through his blood vessels to every limb.

"This is..." Chen Ji looked down at his hands, seeing faint golden patterns faintly emerging beneath his skin, as if molten magma flowed through his bloodline. At the same time, a blurry figure slowly formed in the depths of his Mental Sea—

It was a young girl's figure, her youthful features bearing seven-tenths resemblance to him, her eyes filled with anxiety and fear.

Sister! Chen Nian!

Chen Ji's entire body shook violently, nearly crying out. That blurry figure was clearly his sister who had been missing for years—the Chen Nian who was taken by the Holy Sect as the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'!

The Chen Nian in memory was still twelve or thirteen years old, with twin buns on her head, following him around all day shouting 'Brother brother'. But the one before him now was haggard and worn, surrounded by bizarre black chains, her soul seemingly imprisoned by something, ready to dissipate at any moment.

"Niannian..." Chen Ji instinctively reached out, wanting to touch that phantom. His fingertips passed through, grasping nothing.

This was not the real Chen Nian, merely a reflected remnant in the bloodline resonance. Yet even so, that bone-deep attachment and worry still made Chen Ji's heart ache violently.

dialogue.content:
Just then, a faint voice sounded in his Mental Sea,断续续, as if separated by thousands of mountains and rivers:

"Brother... don't trust... Chen Xuan..."

The voice was too weak, ready to dissipate in the wind at any moment. But every word exploded like thunderclap in Chen Ji's mind, causing him to freeze on the spot.

"Niannian! Is that you?" Chen Ji frantically called out within his Mental Sea. "What's wrong with Chen Xuan? What does he want from me?"

However, that figure had already grown fainter and fainter, leaving only a few final words echoing in his Mental Sea: "Be careful... Heavenly Secrets... the true form... he's not..."

The voice cut off abruptly. That figure dissolved completely, as if it had never existed.

text.content:
Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, gasping for breath. Cold sweat had soaked through his undergarments, clinging to his back with icy chill.

The true form of the Heavenly Secrets? What was that? Was the fragment he had seen not the real Tianji Record? Or was there some unknown secret hidden within Chen Xuan's legacy?

Countless questions swirled in his mind, but Chen Nian's words 'don't trust Chen Xuan' were like a thorn, deeply embedded in his heart. Chen Xuan was the creator of the Tianji Record, the starting point of all prophecies—if even this person could not be trusted, then what could he trust?

More importantly—how did Chen Nian know all this? She was clearly imprisoned by the Holy Sect; why could she still manifest through bloodline resonance? Was all this coincidence, or was someone scheming in the shadows?

At this moment, Mo Xiansheng's phantom also fell silent, his weathered face showing an indecipherable expression, as if weighing something in his mind.

Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to regain composure. His sister's warning, Ling Yuan's origins, Chen Xuan's secret—there must be some connection between these three. He needed more time to sort through all this, rather than making wrong judgments in the heat of emotion.

"Mo Xiansheng," he spoke, his voice already restored to its usual calm, "what happened today, do not mention it to anyone."

"This old servant understands." Mo Xiansheng bowed respectfully, "The Young Master's wisdom is discerning. Sometimes, the more you know, the faster you die."

These words made Chen Ji's heart tighten. He turned to look out the window—the sky had already begun to lighten, and without realizing it, he had spent an entire night in this blood resonance.

However, just at this moment, hurried footsteps sounded outside the door.

"Chen Ji! Are you in there?" It was Su Qingyao's voice, carrying suppressed anxiety, "Something big happened! Sect Master Ling Yuan has summoned all disciples—he says there's an important matter concerning the sect's survival!"

Chen Ji frowned. For Ling Yuan to suddenly convene a full disciple assembly at this critical moment—the timing was too coincidental. Was it coincidence, or had he already sensed something?

"I understand." Chen Ji responded, quickly straightening his robes, pressing all the shock and turmoil from before deep into his heart. When he pushed open the door and stepped out, his face had already donned that usual timid appearance—the bulliedtrash waste servant disciple that everyone knew.

But in the instant he turned, his gaze became sharp as a blade. Ling Yuan, what are you planning? Let's see what tricks you're up to this time.

Several hundred disciples had already gathered in the plaza, their voices booming and discussions abuzz. Chen Ji lowered his head, mingling among the servant disciples, completely unremarkable.

On the high platform above, Ling Yuan wore a dark cyan robe, his expression majestic, standing with hands clasped behind his back. His gaze swept across the crowd, seemingly searching for something. When that gaze passed over Chen Ji, it lingered for merely an instant before moving elsewhere.

But in that brief moment, Chen Ji caught something unusual—that gaze carried a certain scrutiny, and also a certain anticipation, like a chess player observing the pieces he had arranged.

"All disciples," Ling Yuan spoke, his voice like a great bell ringing through the entire gathering, "Today I have summoned everyone to announce a major event—the Ancient Forbidden Land 'Tianji Tomb' will open in three days!"

Tianji Tomb!

These three words exploded in the plaza like thunder, and everyone plunged into wild discussion. The Ancient Forbidden Land—that was the legendary place where fragments of Heavenly Dao's will lay buried, its hidden opportunities and dangers equally incalculable.

Chen Ji, however, furrowed his brow. Tianji Tomb, Tianji Record—the connection between these two names was far too obvious. Was Ling Yuan announcing this at this time merely coincidence, or was it deliberate?

"For this opening of the Tianji Tomb, this old man will personally lead the expedition." Ling Yuan continued, "Thirty disciples from the Inner Sect will be selected to accompany me. As for the Outer Sect and servants..." He paused, his gaze sweeping the crowd once more, "Those who have performed exceptionally may also obtain qualification to accompany us."

These words made Chen Ji's heart stir. Exceptionally performed? What was Ling Yuan implying?

choice.prompt: Ling Yuan's words plunged Chen Ji into deep contemplation. Volunteering might draw Ling Yuan's attention, but if he didn't take this opportunity to approach the core of the Tianji Tomb, how could he unravel the mysteries that haunted him?

choices.description: "One cannot catch a tiger's cub without entering the tiger's den." The Tianji Tomb must certainly hold secrets related to the Tianji Record—this was a rare opportunity. Even if it meant exposing some of his abilities, he must争取随行资格.
choices.visible_cost: May arouse suspicion from Ling Yuan and Su Qingyao
choices.visible_reward: Gain the opportunity to enter the Tianji Tomb and uncover more truths
choices.risk_hint: Ling Yuan may be setting up a scheme in the shadows—rushing into the situation may play right into his hands

text.content:
Amidst the crowd's agitation, a timid voice suddenly rang out: "Sect... Sect Master, this disciple is willing to accompany you!"

Everyone turned to look—a frail servant disciple was blushing as he raised his hand, his entire body trembling nervously. Laughter immediately erupted around him.

"Hahaha! Thistrash wants to enter the Tianji Tomb? Perhaps he'll be scared to death by the demonic beasts inside!"

"An ignorant wretch who doesn't know the height of the heavens! Why doesn't he pee on himself first!"

Mockery rang out one after another, but Chen Ji couldn't care less. He lowered his head, the corner of his lips slightly lifting—these people mocked him more, and fewer would take him seriously. Perfect—this gave him the best cover.

choices.description: Being too deliberate would only arouse suspicion. Better to follow secretly and see what Ling Yuan is planning. Perhaps Su Qingyao will actively help争取机会.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the opportunity to enter the Tianji Tomb
choices.visible_reward: Reveal no intentions and maintain the disguise
choices.risk_hint: If Su Qingyao doesn't notice him, he may truly miss this opportunity

text.content:
Chen Ji didn't raise his hand, only standing silently in the crowd, observing the reactions around him.

"Chen Ji?" Su Qingyao's voice suddenly sounded behind him, carrying a hint of doubt, "You don't want to go to the Tianji Tomb? That is indeed a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity."

Chen Ji shook his head with a bitter smile: "Senior Su speaks jest. With my meager abilities, going would only mean sending myself to death. Besides..." He lowered his voice, "The Sect Master seems to have some... special attention for me. I'm afraid getting too close would only bring disaster."

Su Qingyao furrowed her brow slightly, studying him with a thoughtful look. She always felt thistrash junior brother had more to say, but couldn't pinpoint what was off.

Ling Yuan's gaze swept across the crowd and finally landed on Chen Ji.

"Since this disciple is willing, then let us give him a chance." His voice carried no emotion whatsoever, "The selection in three days—all disciples of Outer Sect rank and above may participate. This old man will personally conduct the examination and select the best."

He paused, then added: "Servant disciples who wish to participate need sponsorship from an Inner Sect disciple. Chen Ji, do you have someone willing to vouch for you?"

This statement seemed fair on the surface but harbored hidden blade. Without an Inner Sect disciple's sponsorship, servant disciples had no qualification to participate in the selection. Was Ling Yuan deliberately making things difficult for him, or testing him?

dialogue.content:
Silence spread through the crowd, the surrounding disciples looked at each other, and no one was willing to vouch for atrash.

Just as Chen Ji thought his plan had failed, a cold voice suddenly rang out: "I'll vouch."

Everyone turned in astonishment—Su Qingyao had already stepped out from the crowd, standing coldly before Chen Ji.

"Senior Su?" Chen Ji showed surprise, "Why would you..."

"Don't misunderstand." Su Qingyao cut him off, her voice carrying scrutiny, "I'm just very curious about you. I want to see what a servant disciple凭借 to make the Sect Master personally call his name."

Her gaze was sharp as a blade, as if trying to see through Chen Ji. Chen Ji lowered his eyes, concealing the complex emotions that flickered in his眼底—this woman was becoming ever more sharp.

text.content:
On the high platform above, Ling Yuan's gaze moved back and forth between Su Qingyao and Chen Ji, the corners of his lips slightly rising, as if very satisfied with what he saw.

"Good, since Senior Su is willing to vouch, then it's settled." He clapped his hands, "The selection in three days—may everyone strive for excellence."

With that, he turned and left, that dark cyan back casting a long shadow in the sunlight. In the instant he turned, Chen Ji clearly saw Ling Yuan's lips curve into a meaningful smile—that smile carried a confident resolve to win, as if everything was under his control.

Chen Ji's heart suddenly tightened. He had a strong premonition—this Tianji Tomb expedition was probably a chess game set up by Ling Yuan from the beginning. And he, along with all the selected disciples, were merely pieces on the board.

The crowd gradually dispersed, but Chen Ji stood still without moving. Su Qingyao walked to his side and said in a low voice: "Don't celebrate too early. The dangers of the Tianji Tomb far exceed your imagination—with your strength, entering would mean death."

"Thank you, Senior Su." Chen Ji slightly bowed, his manner respectful, "But there are some things, even knowing death awaits, one must do."

Su Qingyao furrowed her brow, about to press for details, when she saw Chen Ji had already turned to leave. That thin back disappeared into the crowd and quickly vanished at the end of the path.

She always felt something was off, yet couldn't explain why. Thistrash junior brother seemed to hide too many secrets—and every time she thought she was close to the truth, those secrets would slip through her fingers like loaches.

"Chen Ji... who exactly are you?" Su Qingyao murmured to herself, her eyes flickering with complex light.

Returning to his simple dwelling, Chen Ji locked the door and sat on the edge of the bed. His fingers gently stroked the scar on his chest—the mark left when the Tianji Record was activated, now transformed into a faint golden pattern.

The images seen during the blood resonance replayed continuously in his mind: the Chen family ancestral hall, Ling Yuan's back, his sister's warning... all clues pointed to a terrifying truth.

"Chen Xuan... the true body of the Tianji Record..." he murmured, "What exactly is going on here?"

He closed his eyes, attempting to communicate with the Tianji Record once more, only to find that familiar power had become exceptionally weak, as if something was interfering.

Just then, a faint golden light glowed from his embrace—the Tianji Record Fragment had automatically activated. Chen Ji lowered his head to look—the paper's surface revealed a line of blurred characters, as if written using the last trace of strength:

"Tianji Tomb, where truth resides. My true body, sealed within."

"True body? Sealed?" Chen Ji's pupils suddenly contracted, an icy chill rising from his spine to the crown of his head.

The characters on the Tianji Record Fragment flashed and vanished, then the paper returned to blankness. Chen Ji gripped the fragment tightly, his knuckles white.

If what the fragment said was true, then the true body of the Tianji Record—that existence known as "Chen Xuan"—was actually sealed within the Tianji Tomb.

Then where did the Tianji Record power he currently used come from? Was it the fragment's autonomous consciousness, or a piece set in motion by some higher existence?

Chen Nian's warning echoed again in his ears: "Don't trust Chen Xuan... beware the Heavenly Secrets... the true body..."

He took a deep breath and tucked the fragment back into his embrace. The Tianji Tomb expedition in three days—no matter what awaited ahead, he had to go.

To unravel the mystery of his origins, to find his sister, and to understand the truth behind all this.

Even if that truth might be more terrifying than he could imagine.
